title: Henry Heil
text:
Hello! I am a Sophomore at Truman State University in Kirksville, MO. I’m currently pursuing a double major in Statistics and Environmental Science with a minor in Math. My current goals are to develop skills in math, statistics, and data science, and couple that with broader subject matter knowledge in environmental science, which intersects sustainability, ecology, earth science, and public health. I don’t yet have a specific career to aim for after graduation, but I am interested in exploring research.
In the past year, I’ve had the opportunity to attend many departmental seminars/colloquia in agriculture, biology, and mathematics, and several university-wide student research symposia. I’ve gotten some experience in data analysis, fieldwork/experimental design, basic wet lab techniques, and math research/presentation preparation through group and individual projects in coursework. These experiences have made me confident in wanting more experience, and I’m searching for external REU programs for the coming summer that explore the intersections of math and ecology.

title: The Effect of Hay Bales on Arthropod Diversity
text: This was a multi-week lab project in Intro to Ecology. I worked with three classmates, Sydnee Gann, Luke Capps, and Andrew Schroeder, to identify a research question relating to arthropod diversity on the Truman State University farm, gather field data, analyze it, and write a report.

title: The Effect of Hay Bales on Arthropod Diversity
text:
Question and data collection
We wanted to determine if proximity to hay bales had an effect on arthropod abundance and diversity. We sampled, using sweep-netting, transects along two sample plots near to and far from hay bales. We used iNaturalist to ID species.

title: The Effect of Hay Bales on Arthropod Diversity
text:
Analysis
Analysis conducted in Excel. We reformatted our data to conduct t-tests comparing samples and create appropriate plots. We also calculated Shannon’s diversity index, H, and the other thing, E.
